Running recorders side by side on one card does not shorten a step: two or three processes write about 0.72 of one process's answers a second. No concurrent capture is proposed for own_text.py, no new protocol follows from this run, and controlled-bf16-7 stays as it is.

The record does not separate the card's switching between processes from contention on the six processor threads the processes shared; that three did exactly as well as two (117.09 s against 117.55 s for the same ten answers) points to the card, as an inference. What is left under a step's generation is the engine's own work at each token (its decode and its stop and read-back at each of the 212 kept outputs): a lever there is a change of the engine build, or of how the card is shared, which is machine policy and not this seat's; neither is proposed here.
Nothing here bears on the hypothesis; no model was changed and no answer's content was compared or judged.
